property_summary: For any bytes4 interfaceId, c.supportsInterface(interfaceId) must return true only if interfaceId equals type(IAccessControl).interfaceId or type(IERC165).interfaceId; the mutant incorrectly returns true for every interfaceId including unsupported ones.

For any bytes4 interfaceId, c.supportsInterface(interfaceId) must return true if and only if interfaceId equals type(IAccessControl).interfaceId or type(IERC165).interfaceId; the mutant returns true for every interfaceId, violating the 'only if' direction.

For any bytes4 interfaceId, c.supportsInterface(interfaceId) must return false for interfaceId values that are not type(IAccessControl).interfaceId or type(IERC165).interfaceId; the mutant incorrectly returns true for every interfaceId.

For any bytes4 interfaceId that is not equal to type(IERC165).interfaceId or type(IAccessControl).interfaceId, c.supportsInterface(interfaceId) must return false; the mutant returns true for all interfaceIds, violating this rule for unsupported interfaceIds. Since types are unavailable, we hardcode the known IDs with constants.
For any interfaceId, supportsInterface must return true for type(IAccessControl).interfaceId, but the mutant always returns false.
For any interface id, supportsInterface must return true for the ERC165 interface id 0x01ffc9a7 (type(IERC165).interfaceId), but the mutant always returns false.
For any interfaceId, supportsInterface must return true for at least one of IAccessControl or ERC165 interface IDs, but the mutant always returns false.
For any interface identifier, supportsInterface must return true if and only if the identifier matches IAccessControl or IERC165; the mutant returns false for IERC165, violating ERC165 conformance.

For any interfaceId, the reference contract's supportsInterface must return true for exactly the interfaceIds it claims to support (IAccessControl, IERC165) and false for others, but the mutant always returns false, breaking the rule for the supported interfaceIds.
supportsInterface must return true for type(IERC165).interfaceId; the buggy version only checks IAccessControl and returns false for IERC165.
supportsInterface must return true for the interface of a parent contract (IERC165); the bug removes the super call so it returns false for type(IERC165).interfaceId.

For any bytes4 interfaceId that is not type(IAccessControl).interfaceId but is supported by the reference contract (e.g., type(IERC165).interfaceId), the reference returns true while the mutant returns false; the test confirms that for a chosen non-IAccessControl interfaceId known to be supported, the reference returns true and the mutant returns false.

For any non-IAccessControl interfaceId, supportsInterface should match the result of the parent ERC165 supportsInterface; the bug removes the super call and returns false for any such interfaceId, including type(IERC165).interfaceId which is supported by the reference.
For any bytes4 interfaceId, supportsInterface must return true for type(IERC165).interfaceId; the bug removes the super call and returns false for this value.
The reference contract’s supportsInterface must return true for type(IAccessControl).interfaceId, but the mutant returns false because it checks the wrong interface (IERC165).
The reference supportsInterface returns true for type(IAccessControl).interfaceId, while the mutant returns false for that same interface ID.

For any Bytes4 interfaceId, supportsInterface(interfaceId) MUST return true when interfaceId equals type(IAccessControl).interfaceId, but the mutant returns false because it checks type(IERC165).interfaceId instead.

For any bytes4 interfaceId, supportsInterface(interfaceId) must return true exactly when interfaceId equals type(IAccessControl).interfaceId or type(IERC165).interfaceId; the mutant incorrectly returns false for type(IAccessControl).interfaceId because it checks type(IERC165).interfaceId instead.

For any bytes4 interfaceId, supportsInterface must return true when interfaceId equals type(IAccessControl).interfaceId, but the mutant returns false for that value because it checks type(IERC165).interfaceId instead.
For any interfaceId, supportsInterface returns true iff it matches IAccessControl or a super interface; mutant returns the negation, breaking for ids that should be supported.

For any interfaceId, supportsInterface must return true if the id is supported by IAccessControl or an inherited interface; the mutant inverts this, so for ids that should be supported, reference returns true while mutant returns false.

For any interfaceId, supportsInterface returns the same boolean as the logical OR of IAccessControl's interfaceId and IERC165's interfaceId; the mutant inverts this by negating the OR, causing a mismatch for every interfaceId that should be supported.

For any interfaceId, c.supportsInterface(interfaceId) must return the same boolean as (interfaceId == type(IAccessControl).interfaceId) || (interfaceId == type(IERC165).interfaceId); the bug inverts the OR, returning the opposite boolean for every id that should be supported.

For any interfaceId, c.supportsInterface(interfaceId) must return true exactly when interfaceId equals type(IAccessControl).interfaceId or type(IERC165).interfaceId; the mutant inverts the OR, returning false when it should be true.
For any role and account, hasRole must return the accurate membership status stored in the contract; the mutant inverts the result so returns true when not a member and false when a member.

For any role and account, calling hasRole twice must return the same value if the membership state has not changed; the mutant can return different values across calls because it inverts the stored boolean which may be altered by unrelated role operations.
For any role and account where the account is a current member, hasRole must return true in the reference; the mutant inverts the return and returns false, breaking membership reflection.
For any role and account, if the account is not a member of the role, calling hasRole must return false; the mutant inverts the return and returns true.

For any role 'role' and account 'account', the result of hasRole(role, account) must equal the result of hasRole(role, account) when called a second time with the same arguments and no state changes; the mutant inverts the stored boolean but is deterministic, so this property holds for both, but the mutant violates the explicit membership state by returning the negation of the stored value, so we instead assert that after granting a role to an account, hasRole returns true.

For any role and account, if the reference hasRole returns true, then the buggy version's false return violates that membership; conversely if the reference returns false, the buggy version's false matches it. Thus the property 'hasRole(id, user) == (the actual role state)' differs: the reference returns true when a role is granted, but the bug returns false unconditionally.
For any role that has been granted to an account via _grantRole, hasRole must return true; the buggy version returns false, breaking this invariant.
For any role and account that has NOT been granted the role, hasRole MUST return false; the buggy version always returns true, violating this for ungranted role/account pairs.

For any role, the admin role returned by getRoleAdmin should be the one previously set via _setRoleAdmin, not bytes32(0). The mutant always returns bytes32(0), violating this invariant for any role whose admin was explicitly set to a non‑zero value.

For any role that has been granted to at least one account (and thus exists in the system), getRoleAdmin(role) must return the admin role that was set for it at construction, which must be non-zero for PROPOSER_ROLE, but the mutant always returns bytes32(0).

For any role, getRoleAdmin must return the role's stored admin role, not the input role itself. The bug always returns the input role instead, so it fails exactly when the stored admin differs from the input role.

For any role, getRoleAdmin returns the role's admin role as stored in the contract, which must be equal to the admin role set via _setRoleAdmin (or the default admin role 0x00 if not set), and the bug returns the input role itself, violating this when the stored admin differs from the input role.

For any role, `getRoleAdmin(role)` must return the pre-set admin role of that role, else `0x00` for unset roles; the mutant returns `role` itself, breaking the invariant whenever the returned admin does not equal `role`.
